title: Org access flows — compact view, micro-interactions, and error states
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures low‑fi wireframe ideas, micro‑interaction specs, and backlog items for the Org/Team Settings surface that covers RBAC, API keys, service accounts, and a compact audit log view. Goal is a space‑efficient admin console for teams with dense controls that still surfaces safety, recoverability, and clear error states. This is a working doc — lots of open questions at the bottom.

Design principles (working):
- Compact density: support admins who manage >50 service accounts without endless paging; use collapse groups and inline actions.
- Safety-first: destructive operations require clear confirmations and undo affordances (soft-delete + 30d retention).
- Fast keyboard-driven flows: accessible keyboard shortcuts for power users (list focus, quick-create modal).
- Progressive disclosure: show advanced config only when the admin expands an item.
- Auditable changes: every write action links to the minimal audit event (row) and exposes the request id.

Top-level screens to prototype:
1) Org access compact list (default)
   - Table-like vertical list for teams and service accounts; each row shows: name, type (user/service key), last_used (relative), role summary (1–2 badges), status (active/disabled), quick-actions dropdown.
   - Inline mini-expand toggles to reveal details: key creation date, scopes, token rotation policy, linked apps.
   - Keyboard notes: up/down to move row, space to expand, E to edit, R to rotate key.

2) Quick create modal (single-step compact)
   - UX: title + short selector for target (team/service-account), role picker (autocomplete), optional note field.
   - For service accounts: optional dropdown to auto-generate API key or link to external KMS.
   - Micro interaction: after create, show a small toasty with a one-time copy panel for the secret. If admin closes it, store an immutable record in an encrypted vault and surface a one-click re-create action (cannot show secret again).

3) Service account detail flyout (right rail)
   - Compact rails: top section summary, middle: active keys (list with last_used + created_by), bottom: rotation and access policy.
   - Important: inline "rotate" action must show expected downtime (zero for key rotation) and indicate what clients need to change.

Audit log compact view ideas:
- Default: dense list with columns: time, actor, target, action, result (success/fail).
- Row affordances: expand to show event payload + request id + related ticket links.
- Filters: role, team, actor, result, timeframe (last 24h, 7d, 30d) and a search bar that supports request-id and ip: filters.
- Perf note: backfill older logs to blob storage; compact view prioritizes recent 30 days.

Error states and recovery flows (detailed)
- Create key failed (500): show toast with transient error and "Retry" button. Include request-id and link to support. Backfill UI state so admin can re-run creation and get a new secret.
- Delete service account (accidental): soft-delete with undo (snackbar for 10s) + tombstoned resource that can be restored from Audit view. API returns tombstone_id.
- Rotation conflict: if two admins try to rotate concurrently, present merge conflict screen showing both requested expiry/activation times and allow admin to choose which rotation to apply or schedule both sequentially.
- Permission update propagation: when a role change affects runtime permissions (dedicated/different infra), show an estimated propagation ETA badge (e.g., ~2m). If propagation fails, log an audit event and surface a "Retry propagate" action in UI.

Micro interactions and animations (low framerate acceptable for low-fi)
- Row expand/collapse: quick slide + fade (150ms).
- Inline role badges: hover reveals full role name and the most critical permission (tooltip).
- Quick copy secret: show clipboard confirmation + optional "save to vault" button.
- Audit row expansion: smooth height transition and skeleton loader for payload (100–200ms).

Accessibility notes
- Ensure all actions available by keyboard; modals trap focus and return.
- Use aria-live for toasts that contain key secrets instructions so screen readers get the one-time copy warning.

Proposed acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Admin can list teams and service accounts in a compact table that matches API response ordering (support next/prev pagination).
- Create service account flow issues a single secret copy panel; secret is not retrievable after close.
- Rotate key API call accessible from inline action and results in an audit log entry with request id.
- Audit compact view supports filters for actor, action, and date range, and expands row to show raw payload.

Backlog (prioritized) — with rough points (T-shirt):
- [M] Compact list + inline expand (3) — wireframe -> dev handoff
- [M] Quick-create unified modal for users/service accounts (3)
- [S] Copy-once secret modal + vault write (2)
- [L] Audit compact view + filters + expand payload (5)
- [S] Soft-delete and restore flow for service accounts (2)
- [M] Keyboard shortcuts + basic cheat-sheet in UI (3)
- [M] Rotation conflict resolver modal (3)
- [S] Propagation ETA indicator hooked to infra event stream (2)

Unresolved questions and risks:
- Vault design: do we surface a re-create flow or an API to request re-issuance only via support? (security implications)
- Paging vs infinite scroll: large orgs want cursor-based paging for stable anchor — prefer cursors but need backend indexing for stable ordering.
- Retention for soft-deletes: proposed 30 days, legal may ask longer. Confirm with security/compliance.
- Audit data cost: compact view aims to show 30 days by default — need cost estimate for storing additional 90/365 days on demand.

Notes for engineering handoff (what to include in Figma/PRD):
- Annotate all micro interactions with timing and keyboard bindings.
- Provide example API payloads for create/rotate/delete with response request_id.
- Include sample telemetry events for client-side metrics: create_success, rotate_conflict, delete_undo.
- Include low-fi responsive variants for narrow consoles (50% of admins use laptop 1280w) — compact list should collapse badges to a single ellipsized string.

Quick sketch checklist (to attach to wireframe export):
- Row default, row expanded, create modal open, create success toast with secret panel, rotate confirmation modal, delete soft-delete flow (snackbar + restore modal), audit row collapsed/expanded.

Stakeholders to sync with before next round:
- Security: Martin Heller (vault + retention policy)
- Infra: Evan Liu (propagation ETA + conflict resolution)
- Legal/Compliance: Priya Desai (retention requirements for audit/soft-delete)
- SRE: include expected logging format for request_id mapping

Next steps (immediate):
- Samira to produce 3 low‑fi frames in Figma covering: compact list, create modal, audit expand (due 2025-03-10).
- Set 30m sync with Martin and Evan to align on vault behaviour (target 2025-03-07).
- Create initial JIRA tickets and link them here (I will create PROJ-4123 family tickets).

Quick links to mock API examples (for devs):
- Create key response: { request_id: "req_XXX", secret: "<one-time>" } (design expects back-end to mark secret as single-view)
- Audit event: { id: "evt_YYY", actor: "user:alice", target: "sa:billing-processor", action: "rotate_key", result: "success" }

Open UI design TODOs:
- Decide whether to show last_used as a hover calendar vs relative time.
- Micro-copy: single view secret disclaimer copy needs legal review.
- Decide if API key rows should show an "attached apps" pill (privacy implications).

End — append wireframe screenshots and Figma link after next iteration.
